items.title: Jerry Gordon interviewed by Monk Rowe and Christian Goodwillie, via Zoom, June 30, 2021
items.q: Customers would say that about John Coltrane too.

ctx.x: If someone came into your store and said, “Well I took a chance and I bought a Sun Ra LP and I just don’t get it. I don’t understand it” —

Every day. Customers would say that about John Coltrane too. Now in my record store we had a record playing every minute that we were open. And my, although I was very much into jazz and its culture, I also needed to make money as well. So I did not play avante garde music while I was trying to do business. I might listen to it at home, I might recommend it, but it wasn’t for everybody. So let’s say I was playing a Coltrane album like “Lush Life” and the customers would go, “Yeah, man, I don’t know what happened

to Coltrane. He played so beautifully and the next thing you know he’s playing chicken scratch music. Or he’s playing Chinese music.” Or something that they could no longer relate to and didn’t know what happened to him. Well in Sun Ra’s case people would go, “Oh Sun Ra, no. He’s out there. He doesn’t know what he’s doing. He’s way out you know. I can’t deal with any Sun Ra.” And I’d say, “Let me play you one.” And then I would play an Impulse album from the 50s where Coltrane, you know, I mean where Sun Ra was…
